messages:
Alex: heads-up — p99 tail spike on prod runtime since last night, correlated with large microbatches + KV cache thrash. I opened a quick profile and it's noisy around kernel selection and KV lookup latency.

Alex: quick excerpt from the profiler: 
```
worker=rt-33 | seq_len=2048 | microbatch=16 | kernel=matmul-fused-quant
exec_time_ms: median=34  p95=210  p99=780
kv_cache: lookups=12k/s  evictions=420/s  avg_lookup_ms=2.3  tail_90pct_ms=18
context_copy_ms per-token ~= 6-12ms (spikes align with evictions)
```

Priya: thanks — I reproduced locally with a mixed workload. Root cause looks like the kernel selector occasionally picks a throughput-optimized quant kernel that assumes cheap KV host memcpy. Under eviction pressure those memcpys pile up and stall token emit. I have a repro script.

Sam: +1. This is also a routing policy effect: when microbatch >= 8 we prefer the throughput kernels (they win on avg), but they worsen tail under high concurrent KV churn.

Maria: proposed mitigations (short-term):
1) soft timeout on token generation path = 700ms (emit partial + stop)
2) per-request max_tokens cap for low-latency route: 256 (was 1024)
3) truncation policy: if estimated remaining work looks like it will breach SLO, truncate left context to keep last 512 tokens
4) force microbatch_size=4 and prefer conservative kernels for the low-latency route (accept throughput hit).

Maria: config sketch for the low-latency route:
```
routes:
  - name: chat_low_latency
    slo_ms: 200
    max_tokens: 256
    microbatch_size: 4
    kernel_pref_order: [fusion_fast, quant_safe, fallback]
    soft_timeout_ms: 700
    truncation_policy: tail_context(keep_last=512)
```

Alex: conservatively sounds reasonable. Any numbers on the tradeoff?

Priya: ran a small canary today: with microbatch=4 + quant_safe kernel + truncation we see p95 ~ 140ms, p99 ~ 260ms, but overall throughput (tokens/sec) drops ~18% on heavy gen workloads. Tail variance reduces a lot.

Sam: ops note — also recommend temporary KV-cache hysteresis: bump cache allocation +10% on canary nodes to reduce eviction storms while we test. That avoids oscillation between cache thrash and kernel fallback.

Deploy Bot: deploy: canary-rt-2026-03-17 rolled to 3 nodes — start_ts=1762001320 — route=chat_low_latency

Maria: action items:
- Priya: run 48h canary perf + regression tests vs existing workload (owner Priya)
- Sam: add KV eviction hysteresis flag and the microbatch override in routing (owner Sam)
- Alex: coordinate a small set of customers for opt-in to stricter max_tokens & truncation (owner Alex)
Timeline: try to complete canary + initial metrics in 48h. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks all — I'll post updates to the incidents channel if we see regressions.
